title: Amana Furnace Code E4: Open High-Limit Switch
meaning: The furnace overheated and the high-limit safety switch shut it down to prevent damage or fire.
diySteps: Turn off the furnace at the switch.
Check the air filter; replace if dirty.
Open all supply vents.
Restore power and see if the code clears.
whenToCallPro: If the code returns after a filter change, the blower motor or limit switch likely needs service.

title: Amana Furnace Code E0: Ignition Failure
meaning: The furnace tried to light the burners but ignition did not occur after several attempts.
commonCauses: Closed gas valve or supply issue
diySteps: Confirm the gas supply valve near the furnace is fully open.
Check that the thermostat is calling for heat.
Reset power and observe one ignition cycle.
If the ignitor glows but burners never light, stop and call a technician.
whenToCallPro: If the ignitor glows orange but no flame appears, or if you smell gas, call a licensed HVAC technician.

title: Amana Furnace Code E1: Gas Valve Relay Error
meaning: The control board detected a problem with the gas valve circuit and locked out the furnace.
commonCauses: Loose wiring at the gas valve
whenToCallPro: Gas valve and combustion issues require a licensed technician.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.

title: Amana Furnace Code E2: Pressure Switch Failure
meaning: The pressure switch did not close when the inducer motor ran, blocking ignition.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect the vent pipe for blockages.
Check the condensate drain for clogs.
Restore power and test.
whenToCallPro: If the vent and drain look clear but the code remains, have the pressure switch and inducer tested.

title: Amana Furnace Code E3: Inducer Motor Fault
meaning: The inducer motor did not start or reach the speed needed to vent combustion gases.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Listen for humming without the fan spinning.
Check the exhaust vent outlet for blockages.
Do not force a seized motor.
whenToCallPro: If the motor will not start after clearing the vent, schedule inducer motor service.

title: Amana Furnace Code E5: Flame Sensor Issue
meaning: The flame sensor did not detect a stable flame after ignition.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Locate the thin metal rod near the burners.
Gently clean the rod with fine steel wool.
Reinstall and run a heat cycle.
whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not help after two attempts, the sensor or gas valve may need diagnosis.

title: Amana Furnace Code E6: Rollout Switch Open
meaning: The rollout switch tripped because flames or excessive heat reached the front of the burner area.
whenToCallPro: Rollout conditions involve combustion safety. Do not reset repeatedly without inspection.
dangerNote: If you smell gas or see soot around the furnace, leave the area and call a technician immediately.

title: Amana Furnace Code E7: Low Flame Signal
meaning: The control board detected a weak or unstable flame after ignition.
diySteps: Turn off power and inspect the flame sensor for soot.
Confirm the gas valve is fully open.
Restore power and watch one ignition cycle.
whenToCallPro: Persistent low flame signals often require gas pressure testing and burner service.

title: Amana Furnace Code E8: Igniter Circuit Fault
meaning: The control board could not energize the hot-surface ignitor properly.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect the ignitor for visible cracks.
Check that the ignitor plug is seated firmly.
Do not touch a hot ignitor.
whenToCallPro: If the ignitor looks intact but the code persists, board or wiring diagnosis is needed.

title: Amana Furnace Code E9: Grounding or Polarity Fault
meaning: The control detected improper electrical grounding or reversed line/neutral wiring.
diySteps: Turn off power at the breaker.
Do not operate the furnace until wiring is verified.
Check that the disconnect and furnace are properly grounded.
whenToCallPro: Electrical grounding issues should be corrected by a qualified technician.

title: Amana Furnace Code 1 Flash: Ignition Failure Lockout
meaning: One LED flash indicates the furnace failed to establish flame during the ignition trial.
diySteps: Verify the gas valve is open.
Reset power and watch for ignitor glow.
If glow occurs but no flame, stop and call for service.
whenToCallPro: Repeated one-flash lockouts usually mean ignitor or gas valve service is needed.

title: Amana Furnace Code 2 Flash: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
meaning: Two flashes mean the pressure switch remained closed when it should have opened.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect venting for obstructions.
Check the pressure switch hose for water or debris.
whenToCallPro: A stuck-closed switch can prevent safe startup and needs professional testing.

title: Amana Furnace Code 3 Flash: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
meaning: Three flashes indicate the pressure switch never closed during the inducer cycle.
diySteps: Inspect the vent pipe and intake.
Check the small hose to the pressure switch.
Clear any condensate blockage in the trap.
whenToCallPro: If the inducer runs but the switch never closes, replace the switch or inducer.

title: Amana Furnace Code 4 Flash: Open Limit Switch
meaning: Four flashes signal the high-limit switch opened due to overheating.
diySteps: Replace a dirty filter.
Open all supply vents.
Reset power after airflow is restored.
whenToCallPro: If overheating continues, the limit switch or blower may need replacement.

title: Amana Furnace Code 5 Flash: Flame Sensed Without Heat Call
meaning: Five flashes mean the board detected flame when the thermostat was not calling for heat.
whenToCallPro: Unexpected flame requires immediate professional inspection.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.
